source.via: The ARR Responsible NLP Research checklist page, fetched with curl; the page says it was 'Updated for ARR October 2024 cycle'. Section headings and question text are copied verbatim from its h3 headings and bold question paragraphs, in the page's order, with markup removed and whitespace collapsed. The guidance under each question is not copied. The sha256 is of the HTML as fetched.

questions.section: A. For every submission:
questions.title: A1
questions.text: Did you describe the limitations of your work?

questions.section: A. For every submission:
questions.title: A2
questions.text: Did you discuss any potential risks of your work?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B
questions.text: Did you use or create scientific artifacts?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B1
questions.text: Did you cite the creators of artifacts you used?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B2
questions.text: Did you discuss the license or terms for use and / or distribution of any artifacts?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B3
questions.text: Did you discuss if your use of existing artifact(s) was consistent with their intended use, provided that it was specified? For the artifacts you create, do you specify intended use and whether that is compatible with the original access conditions (in particular, derivatives of data accessed for research purposes should not be used outside of research contexts)?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B4
questions.text: Did you discuss the steps taken to check whether the data that was collected / used contains any information that names or uniquely identifies individual people or offensive content, and the steps taken to protect / anonymize it?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B5
questions.text: Did you provide documentation of the artifacts, e.g., coverage of domains, languages, and linguistic phenomena, demographic groups represented, etc.?

questions.section: B. Did you use or create scientific artifacts?
questions.title: B6
questions.text: Did you report relevant statistics like the number of examples, details of train / test / dev splits, etc. for the data that you used / created?

questions.section: C. Did you run computational experiments?
questions.title: C
questions.text: Did you run computational experiments?

questions.section: C. Did you run computational experiments?
questions.title: C1
questions.text: Did you report the number of parameters in the models used, the total computational budget (e.g., GPU hours), and computing infrastructure used?

questions.section: C. Did you run computational experiments?
questions.title: C2
questions.text: Did you discuss the experimental setup, including hyperparameter search and best-found hyperparameter values?

questions.section: C. Did you run computational experiments?
questions.title: C3
questions.text: Did you report descriptive statistics about your results (e.g., error bars around results, summary statistics from sets of experiments), and is it transparent whether you are reporting the max, mean, etc. or just a single run?

questions.section: C. Did you run computational experiments?
questions.title: C4
questions.text: If you used existing packages (e.g., for preprocessing, for normalization, or for evaluation, such as NLTK, Spacy, ROUGE, etc.), did you report the implementation, model, and parameter settings used?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D
questions.text: Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D1
questions.text: Did you report the full text of instructions given to participants, including e.g., screenshots, disclaimers of any risks to participants or annotators, etc.?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D2
questions.text: Did you report information about how you recruited (e.g., crowdsourcing platform, students) and paid participants, and discuss if such payment is adequate given the participants’ demographic (e.g., country of residence)?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D3
questions.text: Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you’re using/curating?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D4
questions.text: Was the data collection protocol approved (or determined exempt) by an ethics review board?

questions.section: D. Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human participants?
questions.title: D5
questions.text: Did you report the basic demographic and geographic characteristics of the annotator population that is the source of the data?

questions.section: E. Did you use AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot) in your research, coding, or writing?
questions.title: E
questions.text: Did you use AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot) in your research, coding, or writing?

questions.section: E. Did you use AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot) in your research, coding, or writing?
questions.title: E1
questions.text: If you used any AI assistants, did you include information about your use?
